who_pays: Sunrun, paying a referral reward out of its customer-acquisition budget - the $1,000 arrives as a prepaid/gift reward card (Visa), not cash.
who_qualifies: Existing Sunrun customers (a separate non-customer program exists); your referee must be a new customer who signs a Sunrun Customer Agreement, gets Sunrun Sign Off within one year, and pays any upfront fees - both accounts in good standing.
work_available: One-time per referee conversion - not work; referrals that never convert earn $0.
what_gets_accepted: A referee who converts: signs the agreement, gets Sunrun Sign Off within one year of the referral, and pays applicable upfront/deposit fees; cannot be someone in the same household (second-home exception).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost; unpaid time is sharing your link and nudging your referee through the months-long solar signup process. Rewards may be taxable (1099).
when_cash_arrives: Never cash - a reward card issued within ~90 days after installation begins on the referee's system; the card is non-transferable, not redeemable for cash, and expires 6 months after issuance.

repeatable.cadence: per referred friend who converts - referrals that don't convert earn $0

demand_side: Sunrun is the buyer - it pays referral rewards to acquire new solar customers; demand is your own network of people considering solar.

who_pays: The State of Indiana, via the Indiana529 plan - a 20% state income-tax credit (up to $1,500/year), not cash.
who_qualifies: Indiana taxpayers (resident or non-resident) who contribute to an Indiana529 Direct Savings Plan account during the tax year - the credit only helps if you owe Indiana income tax.
work_available: Annual: claim once per tax year; not work - a tax reduction for people already saving for education.
what_gets_accepted: Your calendar-year contributions to an Indiana529 account, claimed on your Indiana income-tax return; the credit is nonrefundable (20% of contributions, up to $7,500/year).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No benefit without your own money: the credit is 20% of what you contribute. Non-qualified withdrawals face federal tax plus a 10% penalty; rollovers out of Indiana can trigger recapture.
when_cash_arrives: Never arrives as cash - the credit reduces your Indiana tax bill when you file that year's return.
demand_side: No market - the State of Indiana funds the credit to encourage in-state 529 saving.

who_pays: The Texas Match the Promise Foundation, funding tuition-unit matching scholarships and grants for Texas Tuition Promise Fund beneficiaries.
who_qualifies: Texas resident students in grades 3-9 who are Tuition Promise Fund beneficiaries and tax dependents of a Texas resident, with family income of $120,000 or less.
work_available: Annual, competitive - applications are scored on grades, income, and dependents; qualifying does not guarantee an award.
what_gets_accepted: Approved applications after income verification and at least $50 in Promise Fund contributions during the sales period; awards are tuition units paid directly to Texas public colleges.
costs_and_unpaid_time: Minimum $50 in Promise Fund contributions; unpaid time is the application, the student career essay, and the report-card submission each year.
when_cash_arrives: Never cash - tuition units deposited by end of September, disbursed directly to Texas public colleges for undergraduate tuition/fees only.

repeatable.cadence: reapply each year; the tuition-grant portion is once-only

demand_side: No market - a Texas state foundation program awarding scholarships to qualifying student beneficiaries.

who_pays: The State of Tennessee, matching TNStars 529 contributions at 4-to-1 for qualifying families (up to $500/child/year, $1,500 lifetime).
who_qualifies: Tennessee residents with a child age 14 or younger whose household meets the TIPS income limits.
work_available: Annual qualifying period (applications and deposits through June 30, 2026 for the current period); not work - a match on your own savings.
what_gets_accepted: Deposits you make to a TNStars account by June 30 of the qualifying period - the state matches $4 for every $1 (deposit $25 to get $100, $125 to get the $500 yearly max).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No match without your own money: deposit $25 to get $100; deposit $0 and you get $0. Non-qualified withdrawals face federal tax plus a 10% penalty.
when_cash_arrives: Never arrives as spendable cash - the match goes into the child's TNStars 529 account for education expenses.

repeatable.cadence: each annual qualifying period, up to the $1,500 lifetime max per child

demand_side: No market - the State of Tennessee funds the match to encourage TNStars saving.

who_pays: The State of New Jersey (via HESAA), funding a one-time matching grant of up to $750 for a new NJBEST 529 account.
who_qualifies: New Jersey resident NJBEST account owners with household AGI of $0-$75,000 opening an account for a new student beneficiary.
work_available: One-time per beneficiary; subject to available funding - not work.
what_gets_accepted: The initial deposit to a new NJBEST account (matched dollar-for-dollar up to $750), applied for within one year of funding; up to $750 of the contribution must stay in the account for three years.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No grant without your own money: matched dollar-for-dollar on the initial deposit. Keep the funds in the account three years or the grant is forfeited back to HESAA.
when_cash_arrives: Never spendable cash - the grant goes into the NJBEST 529 account for education expenses.
demand_side: No market - the State of New Jersey funds the grant to seed new NJBEST accounts.

who_pays: AT&T, paying a $100 Visa Reward Card per qualifying FirstNet referral out of its subscriber-acquisition budget.
who_qualifies: Existing AT&T wireless or FirstNet Subscriber Paid customers referring new customers who are eligible for FirstNet (public-safety employees/volunteers, verified within 30 days) and open a new line on an eligible unlimited plan.
work_available: Per qualifying referral, capped at 10 referral cards per customer lifetime - not work; referrals that don't verify or stay active earn nothing.
what_gets_accepted: A new FirstNet line that completes eligibility verification within 30 days and stays active on a qualifying plan (min $54/month) for at least 30 days.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost; unpaid time is sharing your referral link/QR code. The $100 card is not cash (no cash access, expires 6 months after issuance; redeem within 75 days of notification).
when_cash_arrives: Not cash - reward notification within 60 days of eligible activation; redeem within 75 days of notification; the card arrives 3-4 weeks after redemption.

repeatable.cadence: per qualifying referral, lifetime max 10 cards per customer

demand_side: AT&T is the buyer - it pays referral cards to acquire new FirstNet subscribers; demand is your own network of public-safety-eligible people.

who_pays: The State of Kansas, matching 2026 Quest529 contributions dollar-for-dollar (up to $600) for qualifying families.
who_qualifies: Quest529 account owners who are Kansas residents (not minors or tax dependents), with 2025 household AGI above $0 and at/below 200% of the federal poverty level.
work_available: 2026 program year only; capped at 1,000 participants statewide, first-come first-served - applying does not guarantee a slot.
what_gets_accepted: Your 2026 contributions of $100-$600 to the KIDS Contribution Account (no withdrawals during 2026; rollovers excluded), applied for by December 1, 2026.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No match without your own money: contribute $100-$600 of your own funds during 2026. Application by mail with tax documents.
when_cash_arrives: Never spendable cash - the match is deposited to the Match Account by January 31, 2027, usable for the beneficiary's qualified education expenses.
demand_side: No market - the State of Kansas funds the match to encourage Quest529 saving.

who_pays: The State of Maryland, contributing $250-$500 to qualifying Maryland529 accounts (income-banded), via the Save4College program.
who_qualifies: Maryland resident account owners 18+ with a Maryland-resident beneficiary under 26, AGI within the published bands (individual up to $112,500 / joint up to $175,000).
work_available: Annual program (apply by May 31, contribute by Nov 1); not work - a state boost to planned college savings.
what_gets_accepted: The application plus the band's minimum contribution ($25 for $500, $100 for $500, or $250 for $250) by Nov 1 of the application year; receiving a state contribution forfeits that year's Maryland income subtraction on your own contributions.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No state contribution without your own money: minimum $25-$250 per band. Miss either deadline and you get nothing.
when_cash_arrives: Never spendable cash - the state contribution lands in the 529 account for education expenses.

repeatable.cadence: each application year, max two contributions per beneficiary per year

demand_side: No market - the State of Maryland funds the contribution to encourage Maryland529 saving.

who_pays: The State of Rhode Island, granting $100 to a newborn's CollegeBound 529 account - no contribution required.
who_qualifies: Children born to or adopted by Rhode Island families, enrolled before the child's first birthday (or within one year of adoption).
work_available: One-time per eligible child; enrollment must happen inside the one-year window.
what_gets_accepted: Enrollment via the hospital birth worksheet checkbox or the CollegeBoundbaby Authorization Form within one year of birth/adoption.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost; unpaid time is a single form. The grant cannot be transferred, withdrawn for non-education purposes, or moved to another 529.
when_cash_arrives: Never arrives as cash - deposited to the CollegeBound account and disbursed directly to the eligible college later.
demand_side: No market - the State of Rhode Island funds the grant for Rhode Island newborns/adoptions.

who_pays: CollegeInvest (Colorado), matching account-owner contributions dollar-for-dollar up to $500 per program year.
who_qualifies: Colorado resident parents/guardians who can claim the beneficiary as a dependent, family AGI at/below the program-year chart, beneficiary 8 or younger at initial application.
work_available: Annual (apply typically Oct-Dec); subject to fund availability - qualifying does not guarantee the award.
what_gets_accepted: Your own account-owner contributions during the program year (third-party contributions excluded); the award goes to a CollegeInvest-owned account disbursed directly to higher-education institutions.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No match without your own money: contribute up to $500 of your own funds to earn the full $500. Reapply every year with fresh tax forms.
when_cash_arrives: Never spendable cash - the match is deposited in the first quarter after the program year, usable only for tuition/fees paid directly to the school.

repeatable.cadence: each program year, up to 5 annual awards per beneficiary

demand_side: No market - CollegeInvest funds the match to encourage Colorado 529 saving.

who_pays: The State of Nevada, matching Future Path 529 contributions dollar-for-dollar up to $300/year for five years (max $1,500/beneficiary).
who_qualifies: Nevada resident account owners with Nevada resident beneficiaries age 13 or younger (at first application), household income $74,999 or less.
work_available: Annual, first-come first-served subject to funding - qualifying does not guarantee an award; reapply every year April 1-July 31.
what_gets_accepted: Your calendar-year contributions up to $300; the grant is deposited the following January.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No match without your own money: save $300+ of your own funds per year for the full match.
when_cash_arrives: Never spendable cash - the match goes into the beneficiary's 529 account, roughly a year after that year's savings begin.

repeatable.cadence: reapply each year, up to 5 years / $1,500 per beneficiary

demand_side: No market - the State of Nevada funds the grant to encourage Future Path 529 saving.

who_pays: The Bank of North Dakota, matching College SAVE contributions dollar-for-dollar up to $300 per beneficiary.
who_qualifies: North Dakota residents who recently filed a ND state income-tax return as residents, AGI $0-$100,000 (single) or $0-$150,000 (joint), with a beneficiary age 15 or younger.
work_available: One match per beneficiary; BND can reduce or stop the match at any time - applying does not guarantee an award.
what_gets_accepted: Contributions made within 12 months of opening the College SAVE account (opt in during enrollment or apply within 12 months); match funds live in a BND-owned account paid only directly to the school.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No match without your own money: contribute $300 within 12 months of opening for the full $300.
when_cash_arrives: Never spendable cash - the match goes to a BND-owned account, paid directly to the eligible school for qualified expenses.
demand_side: No market - the Bank of North Dakota funds the match to encourage College SAVE saving.

who_pays: FAME (Finance Authority of Maine), funding a $100 Initial Matching Grant into new NextGen 529 accounts.
who_qualifies: New NextGen 529 accounts where either the account owner or the beneficiary is a Maine resident; one grant per beneficiary.
work_available: One-time per beneficiary; ongoing program with no stated end date.
what_gets_accepted: Opening the account AND contributing at least $25 - the grant is awarded automatically after the qualifying contribution, not at opening.
costs_and_unpaid_time: Requires your own $25 contribution. The grant stays FAME property until paid directly to a school.
when_cash_arrives: Never spendable cash - the $100 goes into the NextGen 529 account, payable only directly to an eligible institution.
demand_side: No market - FAME funds the grant to seed new NextGen 529 accounts.

who_pays: Synchrony Bank (Amazon's card issuer), paying an $80 Amazon Gift Card signup incentive to acquire Store Card cardholders.
who_qualifies: New Amazon Store Card applicants with an Amazon.com account who pass Synchrony credit approval; existing cardholders excluded.
work_available: One-time on approval; limited-time offer whose amount can change.
what_gets_accepted: Credit approval - denied applicants get nothing; the bonus lands on approval, no purchase required.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost if you never use the card. Full application = hard inquiry; 29.99% variable APR and up to $40 late fee if you carry a balance - the interest wipes out the $80 fast.
when_cash_arrives: Instantly on approval - loaded to your Amazon wallet as an $80 Amazon Gift Card (store credit, usable only on Amazon).
demand_side: The issuer is the buyer - Synchrony pays the incentive to acquire Store Card holders.

who_pays: Synchrony Bank (JCPenney's card issuer), paying a $10 CashPass certificate (plus first-purchase coupons) to acquire new cardholders.
who_qualifies: New JCPenney Credit Card/Mastercard applicants in the US and PR who pass Synchrony credit approval.
work_available: One-time per account; the first-purchase coupon must be used by 11/30/2026.
what_gets_accepted: Credit approval for a new account; the $10 certificate posts within 48 hours of opening, no purchase required. The $35/$125 coupon requires a qualifying first purchase by 11/30/2026.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost beyond what you already planned to buy. Full application = hard inquiry; 33.24% variable APR if you carry a balance.
when_cash_arrives: $10 CashPass certificate within 48 hours of account opening; both the certificate and coupons are savings on JCPenney spending, not cash.
demand_side: The issuer is the buyer - Synchrony pays signup incentives to acquire JCPenney cardholders.

who_pays: Zales, offering a $50-off code to acquire new email registrants.
who_qualifies: New email registrants; no purchase or credit application needed.
work_available: One-time per new registration; code valid 30 days after the email arrives.
what_gets_accepted: The email signup; the $50 code applies to a single online order of $300 or more.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. The discount only pays off on a $300+ order you already planned - never buy extra to chase it.
when_cash_arrives: Immediately by email - the code is savings on Zales spending, not cash.
demand_side: The retailer is the buyer - Zales offers the coupon to capture new email subscribers.

who_pays: Synchrony Bank/Lowe's, offering 20% off (up to $100) to acquire new MyLowe's Rewards Credit Card holders.
who_qualifies: New MyLowe's Rewards Credit Card accounts (US consumer) that pass credit approval; one coupon per account.
work_available: One-time on the first qualifying purchase with the new account.
what_gets_accepted: Credit approval plus a qualifying new-account purchase; the 20% barcode discount applies at checkout (up to $100 off).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost if the purchase was already planned. Hard inquiry on application; 31.99% purchase APR (36.99% penalty APR) if you carry a balance.
when_cash_arrives: At the first qualifying purchase - the discount is savings on Lowe's spending, not cash.
demand_side: The issuer/retailer is the buyer - the signup discount acquires new cardholders.

who_pays: Citi/Home Depot, offering up to $100 off a qualifying purchase to acquire new Home Depot Consumer Credit Card holders.
who_qualifies: New Home Depot Consumer Credit Card accounts opened by 1/27/2027 that pass credit approval; prequalification is available without a credit-score hit but is not approval.
work_available: One-time on a qualifying purchase with the new account; offer valid on accounts opened by 1/27/2027.
what_gets_accepted: Credit approval plus a qualifying purchase on the new card - store-only card, no ongoing rewards.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost if the purchase was already planned. Full application = hard inquiry; variable APR on carried balances; deferred-interest promos charge interest retroactively if unpaid in full.
when_cash_arrives: At the qualifying purchase - the discount is savings on Home Depot spending, not cash.
demand_side: The issuer/retailer is the buyer - the discount acquires new store-card holders.

who_pays: Department Stores National Bank/Macy's, offering 20% off (up to $100) to acquire new Macy's Card or Macy's Amex holders.
who_qualifies: New Macy's Card/Macy's Amex accounts with immediate approval on the day of application; delayed applications and Macy's employees excluded.
work_available: One-time, valid only on the day you are approved.
what_gets_accepted: Immediate credit approval on application day plus qualifying merchandise purchases that same day (up to $500 planned spending reaches the $100 max).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost if purchases were already planned. Hard inquiry; 25.49% variable APR if you carry a balance.
when_cash_arrives: On approval day at checkout - the discount is savings on Macy's spending, not cash.
demand_side: The issuer/retailer is the buyer - the signup discount acquires new cardholders.

who_pays: MNSAVES (Minnesota 529), funding a $50 Smart Start match into the baby's 529 account.
who_qualifies: Parents/guardians of a baby under one year old who open a new MNSAVES account before the first birthday and use promo code SmartStart26; promotion ends 12/31/2026.
work_available: One-time; the 2026 promotion ends 12/31/2026.
what_gets_accepted: The account opened with the promo code plus $25+/month recurring contributions kept running for six months.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No match without your own money: $50 minimum deposit plus $150 in recurring contributions ($25/month x 6) to unlock the $50 bonus.
when_cash_arrives: Per the promotion's official rules after the six months complete - the match goes into the 529 account for education expenses, never cash.
demand_side: No market - MNSAVES funds the match to get parents saving early.

who_pays: Lamps Plus, offering a $15-off coupon to acquire new-homeowner program signups.
who_qualifies: Anyone who completes the New Homeowner signup form (name, email, zip); no purchase required to get the coupon.
work_available: One-time per signup; ongoing while the offer is live.
what_gets_accepted: The completed signup form; the $15 coupon applies to an order of $50 or more.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Savings on planned spending only - never buy extra to chase it.
when_cash_arrives: On signup - the coupon is savings on Lamps Plus spending, not cash.
demand_side: The retailer is the buyer - the coupon acquires new-homeowner program signups.

who_pays: Hibbett, offering a $10-off coupon to acquire Mobile Alerts (SMS) subscribers.
who_qualifies: Anyone who signs up for Hibbett Mobile Alerts; no purchase required.
work_available: One-time at signup; ongoing while the offer is live.
what_gets_accepted: The SMS signup; the $10 coupon applies to an order of $50 or more (some brands/styles excluded).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost beyond planned spending; you opt into marketing texts.
when_cash_arrives: At signup - the coupon is savings on Hibbett spending, not cash.
demand_side: The retailer is the buyer - the coupon acquires SMS subscribers.

who_pays: Journeys, offering a $10-off welcome perk to acquire All Access members.
who_qualifies: New Journeys All Access members; free to join online or in-store.
work_available: One-time on joining; ongoing while the offer is live.
what_gets_accepted: Free All Access enrollment; the $10 perk applies to a first order of $75 or more.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost; membership is free. Never buy extra to chase the discount.
when_cash_arrives: On joining - the perk is savings on a first Journeys order, not cash.
demand_side: The retailer is the buyer - the welcome perk acquires loyalty-program members.

who_pays: Synchrony Bank (Belk's card issuer), paying $10 Bonus Belk Reward Dollars to acquire new Belk Rewards+ cardholders.
who_qualifies: New Belk Rewards+ credit card accounts (store card or Mastercard) that pass Synchrony credit approval AND make a purchase the day the account is opened.
work_available: One-time per new account.
what_gets_accepted: Credit approval plus a purchase made on day one of the new account; the $10 in Bonus Reward Dollars posts within 10 days.
costs_and_unpaid_time: Requires a day-one purchase (keep it small and already-planned). Full application = hard inquiry; 34.99% variable APR if you carry a balance. Reward Dollars expire 60 days after issue.
when_cash_arrives: $10 in Belk Reward Dollars within 10 days - savings on Belk spending, not cash.
demand_side: The issuer/retailer is the buyer - the bonus acquires new Belk cardholders.

who_pays: YouGov, a survey platform paying points per completed survey.
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account, an honest demographic profile, and PayPal for most payouts.
work_available: Survey-dependent - invitations depend on your demographic profile and are never guaranteed; screen-outs happen but are less common than on other panels.
what_gets_accepted: Completed surveys (typically 50-500 points for 5-15 minutes); you must reach the full redemption threshold before claiming anything.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Unpaid time is filling profile surveys and any screen-outs; the effective hourly rate is very low (the lowest practical US tier is 25,000 points/$15, taking months of casual participation).
when_cash_arrives: Once you reach the reward threshold (5,000+ points; voucher claim instructions emailed after redemption).
demand_side: Market-research firms buy responses through YouGov; demand is researcher need for your demographic profile - invitations are never guaranteed.

who_pays: GrabPoints, a survey/rewards platform paying points per completed survey.
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account, an honest demographic profile, and PayPal for most payouts.
work_available: Survey-dependent - qualification depends on your profile demographics; disqualification partway through is common.
what_gets_accepted: Completed surveys matched to your 'About Me' profile; points at 1,000 = $1, minimum redemption 3,000 points ($3).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Unpaid time is screen-outs (partial points sometimes) and inactivity - points expire after 3 months of no activity.
when_cash_arrives: Redeemable at 3,000 points ($3); official site advertises same-day cashout to PayPal or gift cards.
demand_side: Market-research firms buy responses through GrabPoints; demand is researcher need for your demographic profile - invitations are never guaranteed.

who_pays: Nielsen, a market-research company paying weekly points for continuous device-monitoring.
who_qualifies: US residents 18+ who can install Nielsen's software/app and let it collect browsing and internet-usage data.
work_available: Always available while the panel runs - but the published maximum is $60/year ($30 mobile + $30 computer), a few dollars a month at best.
what_gets_accepted: Keeping the software installed and connected; weekly points credit automatically. Computer-side mostly earns sweepstakes entries, not guaranteed rewards.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. The cost is continuous device monitoring (browsing/usage data, plus call stats on mobile); points expire 1 year after crediting and accounts go inactive after 6 months without eligible devices.
when_cash_arrives: Weekly points, redeemable for rewards up to $60/year; must be 18+ (under-18 credits are forfeited, with only a parental-approval loophole for the computer panel).

repeatable.cadence: ongoing while your devices stay connected

demand_side: Nielsen itself is the buyer - it pays for your browsing and usage data; demand is its panel quota.

who_pays: PaidViewpoint, a survey site paying real cash (not points) per completed survey.
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account, an honest demographic profile, and PayPal.
work_available: Survey-dependent - surveys arrive as you're matched; no guaranteed volume, and pay rises only as your TraitScore rises.
what_gets_accepted: Completed trait and market-research surveys; PaidViewpoint pays per completed survey, even partial ones.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Unpaid time is checking the site multiple times a day and building your TraitScore; even very active users make 'an extra $20 a week' per the site itself.
when_cash_arrives: Cashout minimum $15 first time (then $10, then $5 per third-party reports - not stated on the official site); third-party sources report payout within ~72 hours.
demand_side: Market-research firms buy responses through PaidViewpoint; demand is researcher need for your demographic profile - invitations are never guaranteed.

who_pays: Survey Pop, a survey/tasks app paying per completed survey.
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account, an honest demographic profile, and PayPal for most payouts.
work_available: Survey-dependent - availability not guaranteed; screen-outs waste time for zero pay.
what_gets_accepted: Completed surveys (most take 5-10 minutes); the 'up to $50/day' headline is an explicit ceiling, and actual earnings vary by availability and profile match.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Unpaid time is screen-outs mid-survey; effective hourly rate is low.
when_cash_arrives: Instant cashout once you reach $5.00 - PayPal, Virtual Visa, US bank deposit, or 100+ gift cards.
demand_side: Market-research firms buy responses through Survey Pop; demand is researcher need for your demographic profile - invitations are never guaranteed.

who_pays: Microworkers, a microtask platform paying per approved task (surveys, data entry, app testing).
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account; first withdrawal requires address PIN verification.
work_available: Task-dependent - availability varies; employers approve or reject submitted work (rejected work is unpaid with no recourse).
what_gets_accepted: Tasks completed exactly per instructions with required proof; auto-approval after 168 hours if the employer doesn't review.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Unpaid time is rejected work and the 3-6 week first-withdrawal PIN wait; tasks often pay a few cents for 10-15 minutes. Withdrawal minimum $9 + fees (PayPal 7.5%).
when_cash_arrives: First payout 3-6 weeks (mailed PIN verification); later withdrawals faster once the $9 + fees minimum is reached.
demand_side: Employers post microtasks on Microworkers; demand is employer need for small jobs - never guaranteed.

who_pays: Eureka Surveys, a survey app paying cash (dollars, not points) per completed survey.
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account, an honest demographic profile, and PayPal for most payouts.
work_available: Survey-dependent - you will be screened out of some surveys; the '$50/day' headline is an official ceiling.
what_gets_accepted: Completed surveys, polls, and tasks; balance accrues in dollars (screen-outs pay a 2-cent disqualification bonus).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Unpaid time is screen-outs and low-paying surveys; reaching $5 takes multiple completed surveys.
when_cash_arrives: Instant cashout at $5.00 to PayPal, US bank deposit, Virtual Visa, or gift cards.
demand_side: Market-research firms buy responses through Eureka Surveys; demand is researcher need for your demographic profile - invitations are never guaranteed.

who_pays: Survey Junkie, a survey platform paying points per completed survey.
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account, an honest demographic profile, and PayPal for most payouts.
work_available: Survey-dependent - invitations depend on your profile and research demand, never guaranteed; screen-outs common. The site's own FAQ: 'You will not get rich by taking surveys.'
what_gets_accepted: Completed surveys; some answers go through provider review and points can stay pending for up to one month. Identity verification (photo ID + selfie) may be required before redeeming.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Unpaid time is screen-outs and the pending-review wait; effective hourly rate is low.
when_cash_arrives: At 500 points ($5) - redeem via PayPal, bank transfer, or e-gift cards (bank transfer and gift cards US-only); points can remain pending up to one month under provider review.
demand_side: Market-research firms buy responses through Survey Junkie; demand is researcher need for your demographic profile - invitations are never guaranteed.

who_pays: Branded Surveys, a survey platform paying points per completed survey.
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account, an honest demographic profile, and PayPal for most payouts.
work_available: Survey-dependent - availability not guaranteed; disqualifications happen when your demographic doesn't match.
what_gets_accepted: Completed surveys matched by the Survey Matching Engine (partial surveys may earn consolation points); low-quality or rushed answers can get you flagged.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No money cost. Unpaid time is disqualifications; effective hourly rate is low. Identity/phone verification may be required before cashout.
when_cash_arrives: At 500 points (~$5 per third-party conversion) to PayPal; third-party sources report processing in ~1-2 business days (official page does not state timing).
demand_side: Market-research firms buy responses through Branded Surveys; demand is researcher need for your demographic profile - invitations are never guaranteed.

who_pays: Five Surveys, a survey site paying $5 for every 5 completed surveys.
who_qualifies: US residents 13+ or 18+ (varies), with an email account, an honest demographic profile, and PayPal for most payouts.
work_available: Survey-dependent - disqualifications and half-surveys don't count toward the 5.

costs_and_unpaid_time: Free to file. Unpaid time is documenting the issue (first try resolving it directly with the business - most AG offices require this); false statements can be a criminal misdemeanor.
when_cash_arrives: Complaint filing is immediate; settlement payouts are slow - cases take years, and eligible consumers are notified after the deal closes.
demand_side: State AG enforcement and multistate settlements (find your state's complaint page via naag.org); the 'demand' is your own harm under a covered action.

who_pays: SEC Fair Funds, returning harmed investors' own lost investment money (e.g., the June 2026 Chatham Asset Management Fair Fund order).

what_gets_accepted: A claim filed with the appointed Fund Administrator before the plan's claims bar date, with trade documentation; denied claims get a chance to cure.
costs_and_unpaid_time: Free to file - beware third parties charging to 'recover' SEC funds. Distributions take years and are reduced by taxes, fees, and expenses.
when_cash_arrives: Years after the enforcement action - after the plan of distribution is approved and claims are processed.

demand_side: SEC Division of Enforcement Fair Fund orders; the 'demand' is your own harm as an investor in a covered case.
